sentences.zh: 劾副都統以下，論如律。

translations.literal: He impeached the vice commandant and those below, who were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the vice commandant and those below, who were sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 歷通政司參議、大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of counselor in the Office of Transmission and Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of counselor in the Office of Transmission and Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出為安徽布政使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as provincial treasurer of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed provincial treasurer of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 值大水，被災者四十餘州縣，倉穀缺乏，庫儲不給，勸紳商輸貲各卹其鄉，與官賑並舉，災民賴之。

translations.literal: When great floods struck, more than forty prefectures and counties were affected; granary grain was lacking and treasury stores insufficient; he urged gentry and merchants to contribute funds to relieve their own townships, carried out together with official relief, and the disaster victims relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: When great floods struck, more than forty prefectures and counties were affected. Granary grain was lacking and treasury stores insufficient. He urged gentry and merchants to contribute funds to relieve their own townships, carried out together with official relief, and disaster victims relied on this.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted directly to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was promoted directly to governor.

sentences.zh: 宿州、靈壁以睢河堤堰崩圮，比年患水，紹鏞親往相視，奏請修復；

translations.literal: Suzhou and Lingbi suffered because the dikes and dams on the Sui River had collapsed; floods afflicted them year after year; Shaoyong went in person to inspect and memorialized for repairs;
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Lingbi suffered because the dikes and dams on the Sui River had collapsed and floods afflicted them year after year. Shaoyong went in person to inspect and memorialized for repairs;

sentences.zh: 又築無為州黃絲灘臨江堤千二百餘丈。

translations.literal: he also built more than twelve hundred zhang of riverfront dike at Huangsi Beach in Wuwei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: he also built more than twelve hundred zhang of riverfront dike at Huangsi Beach in Wuwei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先後捕獲鳳、潁等府土匪五十餘人，置諸法。

translations.literal: He successively captured more than fifty bandits in the prefectures of Fengyang and Yingzhou and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He successively captured more than fifty bandits in Fengyang, Yingzhou, and other prefectures and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，詔各直省清查陋規雜稅，紹鏞疏陳，略曰：「廣東州縣所資辦公，專在兵米折價。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Daoguang reign an edict ordered every province to investigate irregular fees and miscellaneous taxes. Shaoyong memorialized in summary, saying: "What funds the prefectures and counties of Guangdong rely on for official business lies solely in the conversion price of military rice.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 an edict ordered every province to investigate irregular fees and miscellaneous taxes. Shaoyong memorialized in summary: "What funds the prefectures and counties of Guangdong rely on for official business lies solely in the conversion price of military rice.

sentences.zh: 因產穀少，民間皆原折納，相沿已久。

translations.literal: Because grain production is scant, the people have all preferred to pay in converted cash, a practice long established.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain production is scant, the people have long preferred to pay in converted cash.

sentences.zh: 在馴謹良民，向依舊規完納，而刁生劣監，不能無抗欠。

translations.literal: Among docile and law-abiding commoners, payment has always been completed according to the old rules, but crafty students and inferior degree-holders cannot be without resistance and arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Docile, law-abiding commoners have always paid according to the old rules, but crafty students and inferior degree-holders cannot help resisting and falling into arrears.

sentences.zh: 有於正數之內絲毫無餘者，更有於正賦之內收不足數者，州縣往往​​以贏補絀，自行償補。

translations.literal: Some pay not a whit beyond the proper amount, while others pay less than the proper levy within the regular tax; prefectures and counties often use surplus to cover shortfall and make up the difference themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Some pay not a whit beyond the proper amount, while others pay less than the proper levy. Prefectures and counties often use surplus to cover shortfall and make up the difference themselves.

sentences.zh: 今若定為折收額數，則所浮之價，悉為應輸之額，其掛欠代償，恐較前益甚。

translations.literal: If a fixed conversion quota is now set, the inflated price will all become the amount due, and arrears and compensations will probably be worse than before.
translations.idiomatic: If a fixed conversion quota is now set, the inflated price will all become the amount due, and arrears and compensations will probably be worse than before.

sentences.zh: 況貪官污吏，視所加者為分內應得之數，以所未加者為設法巧取之數。

translations.literal: Moreover corrupt officials treat what has been added as their rightful due and what has not yet been added as sums to be taken by devious means.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover corrupt officials treat what has been added as their rightful due and what has not yet been added as sums to be taken by devious means.

sentences.zh: 雍正時將地丁火耗酌給養廉，議者謂正賦之外又加正賦，將來恐耗羨之外又加耗羨。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign land tax surcharges were allotted for supplemental salaries; debaters said that on top of the regular levy another regular levy was added, and feared that in future beyond the surcharge there would be another surcharge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng reign land tax surcharges were allotted for supplemental salaries. Debaters said that on top of the regular levy another regular levy was added and feared that in future beyond the surcharge there would be another surcharge.

sentences.zh: 八九十年以來，錢糧火耗，視昔有加，不出前人所慮。

translations.literal: Over the past eighty or ninety years grain-tax surcharges have increased compared with the past, exactly as the earlier critics feared.
translations.idiomatic: Over the past eighty or ninety years grain-tax surcharges have increased compared with the past, exactly as earlier critics feared.

sentences.zh: 兵米折價，與之事實相近。

translations.literal: The conversion price of military rice closely resembles this situation.
translations.idiomatic: The conversion price of military rice closely resembles this situation.

sentences.zh: 即能明察暗訪，堅持於數年之間，斷難遠慮周防，遙制於數十年之後。

translations.literal: Even with keen inspection and secret investigation maintained for several years, it is impossible to plan far ahead with comprehensive prevention and control matters decades later.
translations.idiomatic: Even with keen inspection and secret investigation maintained for several years, it is impossible to plan far ahead with comprehensive prevention and control matters decades later.

sentences.zh: 至雜稅及舟車、行戶、鹽當、規禮等款，名目不一，或此有而彼無，或此多而彼寡，願者減其數以求悅，黠者浮其數以取贏。

translations.literal: As for miscellaneous taxes and items such as boats and carts, shops, salt houses, and customary gifts, the names are not uniform—some places have them and others do not, some have more and others less; the willing reduce the figures to please, the crafty inflate the figures to profit.
translations.idiomatic: As for miscellaneous taxes and items such as boats and carts, shops, salt houses, and customary gifts, the names are not uniform. Some places have them and others do not, some have more and others less. The willing reduce the figures to please; the crafty inflate the figures to profit.

sentences.zh: 究之浮者即浮，數已定而難改；

translations.literal: In the end what was inflated remains inflated, the figure once fixed is hard to change;
translations.idiomatic: In the end what was inflated remains inflated; the figure once fixed is hard to change;

sentences.zh: 減者非減，事甫過而仍加。

translations.literal: what was reduced was not truly reduced, and once the matter passed the levies were raised again.
translations.idiomatic: what was reduced was not truly reduced, and once the matter passed the levies were raised again.

sentences.zh: 此時毫髮未盡之遺，即將來積重難返之漸。

translations.literal: At this time, even the slightest remnant left unpaid is the beginning of a future accumulation that will be hard to reverse.
translations.idiomatic: The smallest unpaid residue left now becomes the first step toward an entrenched burden that will later be impossible to undo.

sentences.zh: 其中更有強狡之徒，向不完納平餘，致饋規禮。

translations.literal: Among them are moreover forceful and cunning persons who never fully pay the surcharges and instead offer customary gifts.
translations.idiomatic: There are especially brazen men who routinely fail to remit surcharges in full and resort instead to customary gifts.

sentences.zh: 今以案經奏定，在有司視為當然，在小民視為非舊，兩相脅制，互為告訐，既不能指為官吏分外婪索，予以糾彈；

translations.literal: Now that the case has been approved by memorial, officials regard it as a matter of course while common people regard it as not the old practice; the two sides constrain each other and lodge mutual accusations; one can neither charge officials with excessive extortion and impeach them;
translations.idiomatic: Since the arrangement has been memorialized and approved, officials treat it as routine while commoners see it as an unwelcome novelty; each side holds the other in check through mutual denunciation—officials cannot be impeached for demanding more than their due,

sentences.zh: 又不能因民間不繳陋規，懲以官法：寬嚴兩窮。

translations.literal: Nor can one punish by official law those among the people who refuse to pay the customary fees: one is trapped between leniency and severity.
translations.idiomatic: But neither can the government punish commoners who refuse to pay these customary fees: lenience and severity alike offer no way out.

sentences.zh: 是雜稅諸項之難於清釐，較兵米折價尤甚。

translations.literal: Thus the difficulty of clearing away these miscellaneous levies is even greater than that of converting military grain rations to cash.
translations.idiomatic: This is why clearing away the miscellaneous levies is even harder than converting military grain payments to cash equivalents.

sentences.zh: 且各項所入，既名陋規，逐款臚列，上瀆聖聽，於國家體制，亦殊未協。

translations.literal: Moreover, since these receipts are called "customary fees," to list each item in detail would affront the Sacred Ear and is quite incompatible with the dignity of state institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to catalog each receipt under the name of "customary fees" would profane the emperor's attention and clash with the proprieties of the state.

sentences.zh: 事有窒礙，不敢不據實密陳。

translations.literal: The matter has obstacles; I dare not fail to report the truth in a confidential memorial.
translations.idiomatic: For these reasons I find the matter obstructed at every turn, and I cannot but report the facts candidly in a confidential submission.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，與兩江總督孫玉庭所議同，其事遂寢。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was received, it agreed with the recommendations of Sun Yuting, Governor-General of Liangjiang, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and found to agree with Governor-General Sun Yuting's views on Liangjiang affairs, and the proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 二年，召署禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned to serve as acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was called to the capital to serve as acting Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂歸，服闋，授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: He returned on mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home to observe mourning for his mother, he was appointed governor of Guangxi once the mourning period had ended.

sentences.zh: 禁土司科派擾累，懲土民刁訟者，緝治逸匪，邊境稍安。

translations.literal: He forbade native chieftains from making improper requisitions and harassing the people, punished local gentry given to malicious litigation, and tracked down escaped bandits, so the frontier gradually grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: He barred native chieftains from levying unauthorized exactions, punished litigious local gentry, and hunted down fugitive bandits, and the border region gradually settled down.

sentences.zh: 五年，調湖南，編查洞庭湖漁船，以軍法部伍之，盜無所容。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Hunan, registered and inspected fishing boats on Dongting Lake, organized them by military regulations, and left no room for pirates.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Hunan, where he registered fishing boats on Dongting Lake, organized them under military discipline, and left pirates no place to hide.

sentences.zh: 澧州諸湖，上承涔水，下泄洞庭，兩岸悉垸田，地低下，洩水不暢，檄道府率屬履勘疏濬，得可耕田萬四千餘畝，奏蠲淤田賦萬一千餘畝，從之。

translations.literal: The lakes around Lizhou receive the Censhui River above and discharge into Dongting below; both banks are polder fields on low ground where drainage was poor. He ordered the circuit and prefecture to lead their subordinates in on-site surveys and dredging, recovered more than fourteen thousand mu of arable land, memorialized for remission of land tax on more than eleven thousand mu of silted fields, and the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The lakes around Lizhou take in the Censhui River upstream and drain into Dongting Lake downstream; both banks were low-lying polder farmland with poor drainage. He ordered the circuit and prefectural officials to survey the ground and dredge the channels, reclaimed more than fourteen thousand mu of arable land, and memorialized for tax remission on over eleven thousand mu of silted fields—the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 九年，入覲，面陳苗疆設立苗弁額數過多，倚勢虐使苗人，易激事端，請酌其可並省者，缺出不補，總督意不合，格不行。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he came to court for an audience and stated in person that too many Miao officer posts had been established in the Miao frontier, that they relied on their power to oppress the Miao and easily provoked incidents, and he requested that posts that could be consolidated be reduced and vacancies left unfilled; the governor-general disagreed and the proposal was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, during an audience at court, he argued that the Miao frontier had too many native officer posts, whose holders abused their authority over the Miao and easily stirred up trouble; he asked that redundant posts be merged and vacancies left unfilled. The governor-general disagreed, and the proposal went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 十年，召授光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled to the capital and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 尋值京察，以在湖南任內廢弛，降四品頂戴，休致。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, at the capital inspection, he was found negligent during his tenure in Hunan, demoted to a fourth-rank button, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, at the capital inspection of officials, he was judged negligent during his service in Hunan, stripped of his third-rank insignia for a fourth-rank button, and retired.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: =硃桂楨=硃桂楨，字幹臣，江蘇上元人。

translations.literal: Zhu Guizhen, styled Ganchen, was a native of Shangyuan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guizhen, whose courtesy name was Ganchen, came from Shangyuan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 累擢郎中，遷御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in due course to director and then transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to director and was then transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，出為貴州鎮遠知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he went out as prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 鎮遠民、苗雜居，無紡績之利，募工教織，於是始有苗布。

translations.literal: Han and Miao lived mixed together at Zhenyuan and had no advantage in spinning and weaving; he recruited workers to teach weaving, and only then did Miao cloth appear.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenyuan, Han and Miao lived side by side but had no local weaving industry; he hired instructors to teach spinning and weaving, and Miao cloth was produced there for the first time.

sentences.zh: 大旱，民飢，急發庫藏平糶施粥，郡無殍人。

translations.literal: During a great drought the people starved; he urgently opened the treasury to sell grain at fair prices and provide gruel, and the prefecture had no corpses from starvation.
translations.idiomatic: When a severe drought brought famine, he quickly opened the treasury to sell grain at fair prices and set up gruel kitchens, and no one in the prefecture died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 事畢，自請擅動庫帑之罪，民感其惠。

translations.literal: When the crisis was over, he himself requested punishment for having moved treasury funds without authorization, and the people were moved by his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis passed, he voluntarily asked to be punished for having drawn on the treasury without authorization, and the people were deeply grateful for his care.

sentences.zh: 次年，感稔，爭醵金還庫。

translations.literal: The next year, when the harvest was good, they vied to contribute funds to repay the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after a good harvest, the people competed to raise money and restore the treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 黃平州有盜，或告變，單騎臨之，呼眾縛為首者出，不戮一人，戍五人而已。

translations.literal: There were bandits in Huangping Prefecture; when someone reported trouble, he went alone on horseback, called on the crowd to bind and hand over the ringleader, executed no one, and banished only five men to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits appeared in Huangping Prefecture and word reached him, he rode out alone, summoned the crowd to produce and bind the ringleader, put no one to death, and sent only five men into frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 興義苗閧，大吏已勒兵，桂楨曰：「此苗忿民欺，保不為變。

translations.literal: The Miao at Xingyi stirred up trouble; the high officials had already mobilized troops. Guizhen said: "These Miao are angry at being wronged by the people; I guarantee they will not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao at Xingyi grew restive, senior officials had already mobilized troops. Guizhen said, "The Miao are incensed at being bullied by the local people; I guarantee they will not rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」使人開諭，果服。

translations.literal: " He sent men to explain and persuade them, and they indeed submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent envoys to reason with them, and they duly submitted.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，治行稱最，擢陝西潼商道。

translations.literal: After three years in office his governance was rated the best, and he was promoted to the Tongshang Circuit Intendant in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office, his record was judged the finest in the province, and he was promoted to intendant of the Tongshang Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 歷浙江按察使，甘肅、山東布政使。

translations.literal: He served successively as provincial judge of Zhejiang and provincial treasurer of Gansu and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as provincial judge of Zhejiang and then as provincial treasurer of Gansu and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調廣東巡撫，卻洋行陋規，遇事執法，外商獨嚴憚之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred as governor of Guangdong, refused the customary fees of the foreign trading houses, enforced the law in every matter, and foreign merchants feared him above all others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Guangdong as governor, rejected the customary fees demanded by the foreign trading houses, upheld the law in every case, and foreign merchants feared him above all others.

sentences.zh: 每月勾捕，不動聲色，臨事集官弁，曰往某所，閭里不擾，莠民斂跡。

translations.literal: Each month he arranged arrests without showing any sign of it; when the moment came he assembled officials and officers, said they were going to such-and-such a place, the neighborhoods were not disturbed, and bad characters withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Each month he arranged arrests without giving any outward sign; when the time came he would gather officials and officers, dispatch them to a named location, and carry out the operation without disturbing the neighborhoods, so that troublemakers kept out of sight.

sentences.zh: 以儉素率屬，一日微服勘災歸，至西關，見千總輿從甚盛，叱止之，千總叩頭請罪乃已。

translations.literal: He led his subordinates by frugal simplicity; one day, returning from inspecting disaster relief in plain clothes, he reached the West Gate and saw a company commander with an excessively large retinue; he shouted to stop him, and only when the commander kowtowed and begged forgiveness did he let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: He set an example of frugality for his subordinates. One day, returning incognito from inspecting disaster relief, he reached the West Gate and saw a company commander traveling with an ostentatious retinue; he rebuked him sharply, and only when the man kowtowed and begged forgiveness did he let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 惠、潮兩郡多械鬥，數興大獄，痛繩以法，稍戢。

translations.literal: The two prefectures of Huizhou and Chaozhou had many armed feuds and repeatedly produced major cases; he punished them severely according to law, and the violence gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou and Chaozhou were rife with armed clan feuds that repeatedly spawned major criminal cases; he punished offenders rigorously under the law, and the violence gradually abated.

sentences.zh: 創議諸郡山場荒地，援雷、瓊例，給照聽民墾種。

translations.literal: He initiated a proposal that wasteland on mountain tracts in the various prefectures, following the precedent of Leizhou and Qiongzhou, be licensed and opened to the people for reclamation and cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that wasteland on mountain tracts throughout the province, following the precedent set in Leizhou and Qiongzhou, be licensed and opened to private reclamation.

sentences.zh: 設鄉約義塾，教養兼施，以弭匪僻。

translations.literal: He established village compacts and charity schools, combining instruction and nurture to suppress banditry in remote places.
translations.idiomatic: He established village compacts and charity schools, combining moral instruction with practical care to curb lawlessness in remote areas.

sentences.zh: 誡僚屬慎刑獄，治民以無冤濫始，每屆秋讞，多所平反。

translations.literal: He admonished his subordinates to be careful in criminal cases, saying that governing the people must begin with avoiding wrongful conviction and excessive punishment; each autumn review he reversed many sentences.
translations.idiomatic: He warned his subordinates to handle criminal cases with care, holding that good governance begins with preventing wrongful convictions; at each autumn judicial review he reversed many unjust verdicts.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以病乞歸，宣宗時時詢其病狀，冀其出。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he requested retirement on grounds of illness; Emperor Xuanzong frequently inquired after his condition, hoping he would return to service.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he retired on grounds of illness; Emperor Xuanzong repeatedly inquired after his health, hoping he would return to office.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒，詔嘉「居官清正，勤政愛民」，依總督例優恤，賜其子鎮舉人，諡莊恪，祀鎮遠名宦祠。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died; an edict praised him as "upright in office, diligent in government, and loving toward the people," granted preferential posthumous honors according to the precedent for governors-general, bestowed the juren degree on his son Zhen, gave him the posthumous title Zhuangke, and enshrined him in the shrine of eminent officials at Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year. An edict commended his "integrity in office, diligence in government, and care for the people," granted him posthumous honors on the scale accorded governors-general, conferred the juren degree on his son Zhen, gave him the posthumous title Zhuangke, and enshrined him in the shrine of distinguished officials at Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: =陳鑾=陳鑾，字芝楣，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: Chen Luan, styled Zhimei, was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Luan, whose courtesy name was Zhimei, came from Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi as one of the top three graduates and was appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi who ranked among the top three graduates of his year, he was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光五年，出為江蘇松江知府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Daoguang reign he went out as prefect of Songjiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daoguang he was appointed prefect of Songjiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 創行海運，鑾駐上海，多所贊助。

translations.literal: When sea transport was first instituted, Luan was stationed at Shanghai and gave much assistance.
translations.idiomatic: When sea transport was first introduced, Luan was stationed at Shanghai and contributed greatly to the effort.

sentences.zh: 署江寧，值下河諸縣水災，流民劫掠，預設防禁。

translations.literal: While acting in Jiangning, when the lower-river counties suffered flood disasters and displaced people turned to plunder, he set preventive restrictions in advance.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as acting governor of Jiangning, floods struck the lower-river counties and displaced people turned to looting; he put preventive measures in place ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 設賑廠郊外，議宜散不宜聚，分各縣留養，大縣二千人，小縣千人，賑畢資遣，竟事無譁。

translations.literal: He set up relief stations outside the cities and argued that dispersing was better than gathering; each county was assigned to retain and support refugees—two thousand in large counties and one thousand in small ones—and after relief they were given travel funds and sent home; when all was done there was no disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He established relief stations outside the cities, arguing that refugees should be dispersed rather than concentrated; each county was assigned quotas for shelter and support—two thousand in large counties, one thousand in small ones—and after relief the refugees were given travel funds and sent home; the operation ended without disorder.

sentences.zh: 調蘇州，歷蘇松太道、江西糧道、蘇松糧道、廣東鹽運使、浙江按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou and served successively as Suzhou-Songjiang-Tai Circuit Intendant, Jiangxi Grain Intendant, Suzhou-Songjiang Grain Intendant, Guangdong Salt Controller, and Zhejiang provincial judge, and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou and went on to hold the posts of Suzhou-Songjiang-Tai Circuit intendant, Jiangxi grain intendant, Suzhou-Songjiang grain intendant, Guangdong salt controller, and Zhejiang provincial judge, and also served as acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 水災治賑，親勘災湖州，諏訪土人，知湖高於田，漊港宣洩不暢，規建堤防，修築垸岸，以保田疇。

translations.literal: In managing flood relief he personally inspected the disaster in Huzhou, consulted local people, learned that the lake lay higher than the fields and that drainage channels did not discharge freely, and planned dikes and the repair of polder banks to protect the farmland.
translations.idiomatic: While managing flood relief he personally inspected the damage in Huzhou, consulted local residents, learned that the lake stood higher than the surrounding fields and that drainage channels were blocked, and planned dikes and polder embankments to protect the farmland.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷江西布政使，調江蘇，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangxi, then to Jiangsu, where he acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as provincial treasurer, then to Jiangsu, where he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 鑾自為諸生時，兩江總督百齡闢佐幕，歷官江蘇最久，周知利病。

translations.literal: From the time Luan was a licentiate, Governor-General Bai Ling recruited him to his staff; he served longest in Jiangsu and knew its advantages and ills thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: From his days as a licentiate, Governor-General Bai Ling had recruited Luan to his staff; having served longest in Jiangsu, he knew the province's strengths and weaknesses inside out.

sentences.zh: 會陶澍、林則徐先後為督撫，百廢俱舉，凡治漕，治運，濬吳淞江、劉河、白茆河，修寶山、華亭海塘，鑾並在事，澍、則徐皆倚如左右手。

translations.literal: When Tao Shu and Lin Zexu served successively as governor-general and governor, neglected tasks were all taken up; whether managing the grain transport, managing shipping, dredging the Wusong River, Liu River, and Baimao River, or repairing the sea walls of Baoshan and Huating, Luan was involved in all of them, and both Tao and Lin relied on him as on their right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Shu and Lin Zexu served successively as governor-general and governor, long-neglected projects were taken up across the board—grain transport, shipping, dredging the Wusong, Liu, and Baimao rivers, repairing the sea walls at Baoshan and Huating—and Luan was involved in all of them; both Tao and Lin relied on him as indispensable aides.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was elevated to the governorship of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，復調江蘇。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred back to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred back to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十九年，陶澍以病解職，代署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Tao Shu resigned on grounds of illness, and Luan acted in his place as Governor-General of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when Tao Shu resigned on grounds of illness, Luan served as acting Governor-General of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 方嚴煙禁，籌海防，甚被倚畀。

translations.literal: At the time he was strictly enforcing the opium ban and planning coastal defense, and was greatly relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was rigorously enforcing the opium ban and planning coastal defenses, and the court placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「自嘉慶以來，鄉曲細民多受邪教誘脅，為風俗人心之害，由於正教不明。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Since the Jiaqing reign, many common people in the countryside have been lured and coerced by heterodox sects, harming customs and hearts and minds, because orthodox teaching is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Since the Jiaqing reign, many common people in the countryside have been lured into heterodox sects, corrupting local morals—a problem rooted in the failure of orthodox teaching to reach them.

sentences.zh: 請敕儒臣闡明聖諭廣訓，黜異端之旨，撰為韻言，布之鄉塾，俾士民童年誦習，以收潛移默化之效。

translations.literal: I request that Confucian officials be ordered to expound the Sacred Edict and Amplified Instructions, repudiate heterodox doctrines, compose them into rhymed texts, distribute them to village schools, and have scholars and people recite them from childhood, so as to achieve the effect of gradual silent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Confucian officials be instructed to expound the Sacred Edict and its Amplified Instructions, repudiate heterodox doctrines, render them in rhymed verse, distribute them to village schools, and have children of gentry and commoners memorize them from an early age, so that moral reform may take hold by degrees.

sentences.zh: 」特詔允之。

translations.literal: " A special edict approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict specially approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，卒於官，贈太子少保，依尚書例優恤。

translations.literal: That winter he died in office; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted preferential posthumous honors according to the precedent for ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office that winter and was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous honors on the scale accorded a minister.

sentences.zh: 賜其子慶涵舉人，慶滋，光緒中官至江西按察使。

translations.literal: His son Qinghan was granted the juren degree; Qingzi later reached the post of provincial judge of Jiangxi in the Guangxu reign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinghan was granted the juren degree; another son, Qingzi, later rose to provincial judge of Jiangxi during the Guangxu reign.

sentences.zh: =吳其濬=吳其濬，字瀹齋，河南固始人。

translations.literal: Wu Qijun, styled Yuezhai, was a native of Gushi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qijun, whose courtesy name was Yuezhai, came from Gushi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父烜，兄其彥，並由翰林官至侍郎，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: His father Xuan and his elder brother Qiyan both rose from the Hanlin Academy to vice minister and repeatedly held control over literary examinations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan and his elder brother Qiyan both rose from the Hanlin Academy to vice minister and repeatedly presided over the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 其濬初以舉人納貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: Qijun first entered the Grand Secretariat as a secretary by purchasing the office with his juren degree.
translations.idiomatic: Qijun first entered government as a Grand Secretariat secretary, having purchased the post with his juren degree.

sentences.zh: ，成一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: , he then passed the jinshi as the top graduate of the first class and was appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the jinshi examination as zhuangyuan, the top graduate of his year, and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，典試廣東，其彥亦督順天學政，詞林稱盛事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he served as chief examiner in Guangdong while Qiyan also served as educational commissioner of Shuntian; the Hanlin circle called it a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he served as chief examiner in Guangdong while his brother Qiyan served as educational commissioner of Shuntian; the Hanlin Academy hailed the coincidence as a notable family honor.

sentences.zh: 道光初，直南書房，督湖北學政，歷洗馬、鴻臚寺卿、通政司副使，超遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign he served in the Southern Library, supervised educational affairs in Hubei, passed through the posts of palace aide, Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and was promoted out of turn to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he served in the Southern Library and supervised educational affairs in Hubei; he went on to hold the posts of palace aide, Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission before being promoted out of turn to Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢兵部侍郎，督江西學政，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War, supervised educational affairs in Jiangxi, and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War, served as educational commissioner of Jiangxi, and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十年，偕侍郎麟魁赴湖北按事，總督週天爵嫉惡嚴，用候補知縣楚鏞充督署讞員，制非刑逼供，囚多死，為言官論劾，大冶知縣孔廣義列狀訐之，訊鞫皆實，復得楚鏞榷鹽稅貪酷，及天爵子光岳援引外委韓雲邦為巡捕事，天爵論褫職戍伊犁，革光岳舉人，鏞荷校，期滿發烏魯木齊充苦役，巡撫伍長華以下降黜有差。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he went with Vice Minister Lin Kui to Hubei to investigate affairs; Governor Zhou Tianjue was severe and harsh in his hatred of evil, employed the expectant magistrate Chu Yong as a judicial officer in the governor's office, used illegal torture to extract confessions, and many prisoners died; censors impeached him; Daye Magistrate Kong Guangyi submitted a detailed accusation; investigation proved all true; it was further found that Chu Yong was greedy and cruel in levying salt taxes, and that Tianjue's son Guangyue had improperly appointed the outside deputy Han Yunbang as a patrol officer; Tianjue was sentenced to dismissal and exile to Yili, Guangyue was stripped of his juren degree, Yong was placed in the cangue and after the term sent to Urumqi for hard labor, and Governor Wu Changhua and those below were demoted to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he went with Vice Minister Lin Kui to Hubei to investigate official misconduct. Governor Zhou Tianjue was notoriously harsh; he appointed the expectant magistrate Chu Yong as a judicial officer in his yamen, used illegal torture to extract confessions, and many prisoners died in custody. Censors impeached him, and Daye Magistrate Kong Guangyi submitted a detailed accusation. The investigation confirmed every charge: Chu Yong had been greedy and brutal in collecting salt taxes, and Tianjue's son Guangyue had improperly appointed the outside deputy Han Yunbang as a patrol officer. Tianjue was stripped of office and exiled to Yili; Guangyue lost his juren degree; Chu Yong was placed in the cangue and, after his term, sent to Urumqi for hard labor; and Governor Wu Changhua and other officials were demoted to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 命其濬署湖廣總督，尋授湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: Qijun was ordered to act as Governor-General of Huguang and soon afterward was appointed governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qijun was appointed acting Governor-General of Huguang and soon afterward was confirmed as governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，崇陽逆匪鍾人傑作亂，進窺巴陵，其濬偕署提督台湧赴岳州防剿，檄鎮筸兵分佈臨湘、平江諸隘，其濬移駐湘陰，賊襲平江，擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the rebel bandit Zhong Renjie of Chongyang rose in revolt and advanced to threaten Baling; Qijun went with Acting Provincial Commander Tai Yong to Yuezhou to defend and suppress them, ordered Zhen'gan troops distributed at the passes of Linxiang and Pingjiang, moved his headquarters to Xiangyin, and when the bandits attacked Pingjiang he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the rebel Zhong Renjie of Chongyang rose in revolt and advanced toward Baling. Qijun joined Acting Provincial Commander Tai Yong at Yuezhou to organize the defense, dispatched Zhen'gan troops to garrison the passes at Linxiang and Pingjiang, and moved his headquarters to Xiangyin; when the rebels struck Pingjiang, he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 及人傑就擒，餘黨竄湖南者以次捕誅，被優敘。

translations.literal: When Renjie was captured, the remaining followers who had fled into Hunan were captured and executed one after another, and Qijun received special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: After Renjie was captured, the remaining rebels who had fled into Hunan were hunted down and executed in turn, and Qijun received special commendation for his service.

sentences.zh: 部議裁冗兵，其濬疏言：「湖南地逼苗疆，人情易擾。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated on cutting redundant troops; Qijun memorialized, saying: "Hunan borders the Miao frontier and the temperament of the people is easily disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry proposed cutting redundant troops, Qijun memorialized: "Hunan borders the Miao frontier, and local conditions are easily unsettled.

sentences.zh: 裁者無多，徒生驕卒之疑，而啟苗、瑤之伺。

translations.literal: The number to be cut is not large; it would only breed suspicion among arrogant soldiers and open an opportunity for the Miao and Yao to watch for weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed cuts are modest, yet they would only breed resentment among the troops and invite the Miao and Yao to test our defenses.

sentences.zh: 」總督裕泰尋定議苗疆近地並仍舊額。

translations.literal: " Governor-General Yutai soon decided that areas near the Miao frontier should all retain their former troop quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yutai soon ruled that garrisons near the Miao frontier should retain their existing troop quotas.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調浙江，未行，武岡匪徒聚眾阻米出境，戕知州，捕治如律。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to Zhejiang; before he departed, bandits at Wugang gathered a crowd to block grain from leaving the prefecture, killed the prefect, and were captured and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to Zhejiang; before he could depart, bandits at Wugang rallied a mob to block grain exports, murdered the prefect, and were captured and punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 奏請於洪崖洞設巡卡，編保甲，以靖禍萌。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting patrol posts at Hongyadong and the organization of the baojia system to quell the beginnings of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for patrol posts at Hongyadong and the organization of the baojia system to suppress unrest before it could spread.

sentences.zh: 尋調雲南巡撫，署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred as governor of Yunnan and acted as Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Yunnan as governor and also served as acting Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調福建，又調山西，兼管鹽政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Fujian, then to Shanxi, where he also supervised salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Fujian and then to Shanxi, where he also took charge of salt administration.

sentences.zh: 奏裁公費一萬兩，嚴捕煙販，時稱其清勤。

translations.literal: He memorialized to cut ten thousand taels of official expenses, strictly arrested opium traffickers, and at the time he was praised for integrity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to cut ten thousand taels from official expenses, cracked down on opium traffickers, and was widely praised for his integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保，照例賜卹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous honors according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with the usual posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 尋復以其濬在山西裁革鹽規，潔己奉公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was further noted that Qijun had abolished salt-custom fees in Shanxi and kept himself pure while serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon added that Qijun had abolished illicit salt fees in Shanxi and had served with scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 特加恩子孫以彰清節：子元禧主簿，崇恩知縣，榮禧通判，皆即選；

translations.literal: Special favor was granted to his descendants to honor his integrity: his sons Yuanxi as registrar, Chong'en as magistrate, and Rongxi as subprefect were all granted immediate selection;
translations.idiomatic: Special honors were granted to his descendants to commemorate his integrity: his sons Yuanxi, Chong'en, and Rongxi were granted immediate appointment as registrar, magistrate, and subprefect respectively;

sentences.zh: 又賜其子承恩、洪恩及孫樽讓舉人。

translations.literal: His sons Chengen and Hong'en and his grandson Zunrang were also granted the juren degree.
translations.idiomatic: The juren degree was also conferred on his sons Chengen and Hong'en and on his grandson Zunrang.

sentences.zh: =張澧中=張澧中，字蘭沚，陝西潼關人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lizhong, styled Lanzhu, was a native of Tongguan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lizhong, whose courtesy name was Lanzhu, came from Tongguan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 進士，授刑部主事，充提牢廳，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, served in the Prison Office, and was promoted in due course to director.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, served in the Prison Office, and rose through successive promotions to director.

sentences.zh: 執法明允，數從大臣讞獄黑龍江、奉天、江南、山東。

translations.literal: He enforced the law with clarity and fairness and repeatedly accompanied senior officials in reviewing cases in Heilongjiang, Fengtian, Jiangnan, and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Known for clear and fair enforcement of the law, he repeatedly accompanied senior officials in reviewing criminal cases in Heilongjiang, Fengtian, Jiangnan, and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年，出為直隸大順廣道。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of the Daoguang reign he went out as Da-Shun-Guang Circuit Intendant in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he was appointed intendant of the Da-Shun-Guang Circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 奸民倡無生教惑眾，澧中率兵役探其巢穴，得圖卷及名冊，悉焚之，歸正者概不株連。

translations.literal: Evil commoners promoted the Wusheng Sect to delude the masses; Lizhong led soldiers and clerks to probe their lair, obtained maps, scrolls, and name registers, burned them all, and did not implicate those who returned to the orthodox path.
translations.idiomatic: When local agitators spread the Wusheng Sect among the people, Lizhong led troops and clerks to raid their hideout, seized maps, scrolls, and membership registers, burned them all, and declined to implicate those who renounced the sect.

sentences.zh: 署按察使，遷福建按察使。

translations.literal: He acted as provincial judge and was transferred to provincial judge of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting provincial judge and was then transferred to the same post in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 署布政使，授直隸布政使，未之任，調山西，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He acted as provincial treasurer, was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhili, did not take up that post, was transferred to Shanxi, and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting provincial treasurer, was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhili but never took up the post, was transferred to Shanxi, and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢雲南巡撫，於刑獄尤矜慎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and was especially cautious and careful in criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan, where he was especially cautious in handling criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，召署刑部侍郎，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was summoned to act as Vice Minister of Punishments and soon afterward was formally appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was recalled to serve as acting Vice Minister of Punishments and was formally appointed soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，河南洊飢，頒庫帑百萬，命澧中偕尚書文慶治賑務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Henan suffered repeated famine; one million taels from the treasury were issued, and Lizhong was ordered to manage relief together with Minister Wen Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, when Henan was stricken by repeated famine, the court allocated one million taels from the treasury and ordered Lizhong to manage relief operations together with Minister Wen Qing.

sentences.zh: 至，即飭查造丁口，按冊抽查戶口；

translations.literal: Upon arrival he immediately ordered registers of population compiled and household rolls checked against them;
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he immediately ordered population registers compiled and spot-checked household rolls against them;

sentences.zh: 調取籓庫戥抽查賑銀；

translations.literal: he had provincial treasury scales brought out to spot-check relief silver;
translations.idiomatic: he had provincial treasury scales brought out to spot-check the weight of relief silver;

sentences.zh: 令州縣按旬具報錢價，以備考覈；

translations.literal: he ordered prefectures and counties to report grain prices every ten days for audit;
translations.idiomatic: he required prefectures and counties to report grain prices every ten days for verification;

sentences.zh: 劾冒賑之考城令及造報舛錯各員。

translations.literal: and he impeached the magistrate of Kaocheng for fraudulent relief and various officials for erroneous reports.
translations.idiomatic: and he impeached the magistrate of Kaocheng for fraudulent relief distribution and several officials for filing erroneous reports.

sentences.zh: 尋授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 清查交代，定追賠章程，考察鎮道等官失察盜案多寡，分別劾議。

translations.literal: He inspected handovers of office, established regulations for recovery and compensation, examined circuit and prefectural officials according to how many bandit cases they had failed to detect, and impeached them separately.
translations.idiomatic: He audited official handovers of accounts, established rules for recovery and compensation, evaluated circuit and prefectural officials according to how many bandit cases had escaped their notice, and impeached them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 嚴責捕盜，先後獲匪盜七百餘名，治如律。

translations.literal: He strictly pressed the capture of bandits; in all more than seven hundred robbers and thieves were seized and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard for the capture of bandits; in all, more than seven hundred robbers and thieves were apprehended and punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「山東地廣民稠，一遇歉歲，曹州之捻匪，沂州之掖匪、幅匪，武定、臨清屬之梟匪，聚眾每至百餘人，隨地裹脅，蔓延不已。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Shandong is broad in territory and dense in population; whenever a lean year comes, the Nian bandits of Caozhou, the Ye and Fu bandits of Yizhou, and the Xiao bandits under Wuding and Linqing gather in bands often of more than a hundred men, coercing people wherever they go, and spreading without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Shandong is broad in territory and dense in population. Whenever a lean year comes, the Nian bandits of Caozhou, the Ye and Fu bandits of Yizhou, and the Xiao bandits under Wuding and Linqing gather in bands often of more than a hundred men, coercing people wherever they go and spreading without cease.

sentences.zh: 群匪多起於曹、沂，而兗、濟受害為尤甚。

translations.literal: The bandit groups arise mostly in Cao and Yi, while Yan and Ji suffer most severely.
translations.idiomatic: Most bandit groups arise in Cao and Yi, but Yan and Ji suffer the worst.

sentences.zh: 地方官展轉稽延，不能即正典刑，匪徒遂無顧忌。

translations.literal: Local officials pass the matter back and forth and delay, unable to apply the statutory punishments at once, so the bandits lose all restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials pass cases back and forth and delay, unable to apply statutory punishments promptly, so the bandits lose all restraint.

sentences.zh: 惟官不以盜為事，民始敢與盜通聲氣。

translations.literal: Only when officials do not treat banditry as their business do the people dare to communicate with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Only when officials do not treat banditry as their business do the people dare to communicate with bandits.

sentences.zh: 殲厥渠魁，脅從自散。

translations.literal: Destroy the ringleaders and those coerced will disperse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Eliminate the ringleaders and those coerced will disperse on their own.

sentences.zh: 即牧令中亦非無長於緝捕勇敢任事之員，惟大法則小廉，人存則政舉。

translations.literal: Even among magistrates there are not lacking those skilled at arrest and bold in duty; only when great law is joined with small integrity and the right man is in place is government carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Even among magistrates there are men skilled at arrest and bold in duty. Only when great law is joined with small integrity and the right man is in place is government carried out.

sentences.zh: 兇匪之橫行，咎在牧令；

translations.literal: The rampage of violent bandits is the fault of magistrates;
translations.idiomatic: The rampage of violent bandits is the fault of magistrates;

sentences.zh: 牧令之不職，責在上司。

translations.literal: the malfeasance of magistrates is the responsibility of their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: the malfeasance of magistrates is the responsibility of their superiors.

sentences.zh: 」詔嘉勉之。

translations.literal: " An edict commended and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: " The court issued an edict commending and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，依侍郎例賜卹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; posthumous honors were granted according to the precedent for vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; posthumous honors were granted according to the precedent for vice ministers.

sentences.zh: =張日晸=張日晸，貴州貴築人。

translations.literal: Zhang Rizheng was a native of Guizhu in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rizheng came from Guizhu in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-second year of the Jiaqing reign, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Jiaqing 22, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，出為四川敘州知府，調成都。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Daoguang reign he went out as prefect of Xuzhou in Sichuan and was transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 he was appointed prefect of Xuzhou in Sichuan and transferred to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 日晸勤於吏職，刻樹桑百益書以勸民蠶，創「勵節堂」以贍節婦貞女之無依者。

translations.literal: Rizheng was diligent in official duties, had the Baoyi mulberry text carved to encourage sericulture among the people, and founded the "Hall for Encouraging Integrity" to support chaste widows and virtuous women without support.
translations.idiomatic: Rizheng was diligent in office, had the Baoyi mulberry text carved to encourage sericulture, and founded the Hall for Encouraging Integrity to support chaste widows and virtuous women without support.

sentences.zh: 政暇，招諸生於署，講析經義、語錄。

translations.literal: In his spare time from government he gathered students at his yamen to lecture on classical meaning and recorded sayings.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time from government he gathered students at his yamen to lecture on classical texts and recorded sayings.

sentences.zh: 郡屬馬邊、屏山等廳縣，毗連倮夷，令附近居民建修碉堡，編聯保甲，民賴以安。

translations.literal: The subprefectures and counties under the prefecture such as Mabian and Pingshan border the Lolo tribes; he ordered nearby residents to build and repair blockhouses and organize mutual-security groups, and the people relied on this for security.
translations.idiomatic: Subprefectures and counties such as Mabian and Pingshan border Lolo tribes. He ordered nearby residents to build and repair blockhouses and organize mutual-security groups, and the people relied on this for security.

sentences.zh: 擢建昌道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to intendant of the Jianchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of the Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十九年，越巂、瓘邊夷匪滋事，偕總兵包相卿督兵平之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Yi bandits stirred trouble on the Yuexi and Qian frontiers; together with Brigadier Bao Xiangqing he supervised troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Yi bandits stirred trouble on the Yuexi and Qian frontiers. Together with Brigadier Bao Xiangqing he supervised troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 招复逃亡，編集練勇，修築碉堡，於要隘建城，以資保障。

translations.literal: He recalled fugitives, organized trained militia, repaired blockhouses, and built walled posts at strategic passes to provide security.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled fugitives, organized trained militia, repaired blockhouses, and built walled posts at strategic passes to provide security.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江鹽運使，再遷湖北按察使，調四川。

translations.literal: He was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Zhejiang, then again to provincial judge of Hubei, and then to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Zhejiang, then to provincial judge of Hubei, and then to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 治獄平恕，不以平反矜能，遇有疑竇，飭另緝改辦，告戒屬吏以哀矜為重。

translations.literal: In handling cases he was fair and lenient and did not boast of reversals; when doubts arose he ordered separate investigation and revision, admonishing subordinates to value compassionate caution.
translations.idiomatic: In handling cases he was fair and lenient and did not boast of reversals. When doubts arose he ordered separate investigation and revision, admonishing subordinates to value compassionate caution.

sentences.zh: 遷河南布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial treasurer of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial treasurer of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河決中牟，值祥符工甫竣，兩次災區二十五州縣，附省災尤重。

translations.literal: The river burst its banks at Zhongmou just as the Xiangfu works had been completed; twenty-five prefectures and counties were stricken in two rounds of disaster, and those near the provincial capital suffered most severely.
translations.idiomatic: The river burst its banks at Zhongmou just as the Xiangfu works had been completed. Twenty-five prefectures and counties were stricken in two rounds of disaster, and those near the provincial capital suffered most severely.

sentences.zh: 每馳詣賑所監視，於郊外隙地捐俸構屋，安戢災黎，遂成村聚。

translations.literal: He often rode to relief stations to supervise, donated his salary to build houses on open ground outside the city to settle the disaster victims, and villages gradually formed.
translations.idiomatic: He often rode to relief stations to supervise, donated his salary to build houses on open ground outside the city to settle disaster victims, and villages gradually formed.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢雲南巡撫，未之任，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan but had not yet taken up the post when he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan but had not yet taken up the post when he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，仍授雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was again appointed governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was again appointed governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 勤於察吏，免銅廠民欠工本銀六千餘兩。

translations.literal: Diligent in inspecting officials, he remitted more than six thousand taels of capital silver owed by the people at the copper works.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in inspecting officials, he remitted more than six thousand taels of capital silver owed by the people at the copper works.

sentences.zh: 在任一年卒，祀四川、雲南名宦祠及鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: After one year in office he died and was enshrined in the shrines of eminent officials of Sichuan and Yunnan and in the local worthies' temple.
translations.idiomatic: After one year in office he died and was enshrined in the shrines of eminent officials of Sichuan and Yunnan and in the local worthies' temple.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：宣宗以恭儉為治，一時疆臣多清勤之選。

translations.literal: Commentary: Emperor Xuanzong governed through respect and frugality, and frontier officials of the time were largely chosen for integrity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Emperor Xuanzong governed through respect and frugality, and most frontier officials of the day were men of integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 帥承瀛等或由卿寺受知，或以守令拔擢，雖間有旋倔旋起、晚置閒散者，其猷為要並可觀焉。

translations.literal: Shuai Cheng Ying and others were noticed from ministry posts or promoted from magistrates; although some were briefly stubborn, briefly restored, or late in life set aside in idle posts, their main achievements are all worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuai Cheng Ying and others were noticed from ministry posts or promoted from magistrates. Although some were briefly stubborn, briefly restored, or late in life set aside in idle posts, their main achievements are all worth noting.

sentences.zh: 硃桂楨實心實政，治績稱最，獨膺易名之典，蓋非幸云。

translations.literal: Zhu Guizhen pursued sincere heart and sincere government; his administrative record was called the foremost, and he alone received the honor of a posthumous title change—this was surely no accident.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guizhen pursued sincere heart and sincere government. His administrative record was called the foremost, and he alone received the honor of a posthumous title change—this was surely no accident.
